symptom: DESCRIBE renders a microflow whose branches cross as `c1 and c2` when the activity actually runs on `not(c1) or c2` — a program that always logs described as one that never does, with mx check clean
cause: Nested if/then/else is single-entry/single-exit; a Mendix microflow is an arbitrary digraph. When an inner split's branch lands where an outer split's branch lands, the describer walks the graph as a tree and emits the conjunction of the guards along one path.
fix: DESCRIBE MICROFLOW ... NORMALIZED (Mode 3): fold the branch guards into one condition via mdl/microflownorm and rewrite a COPY of the graph into the equivalent nested one, then let the existing describer render it. Refuses per-decision when the region holds an activity, a rule-based split, or genuinely interleaved branches.
insight: Do not write a second describer for a second rendering mode — rewrite the GRAPH and reuse the one describer, or the two drift and every activity renderer is implemented twice. Two verification lessons. (1) A boolean simplifier needs a truth-table equivalence test over generated formulas, not per-rule unit tests: an unsound rewrite produces a pretty WRONG guard, which is the original bug from the other direction. Run it with a rule deliberately broken as the control — mine caught it at the first assignment. (2) Algebra is not behaviour: build the original and the microflow rebuilt from its normalized description side by side and compare return values over the whole input truth table on a real runtime. The rows that matter are the ones the OLD rendering got wrong, so make the fixture's return value distinguish them (a `log` activity is invisible to a test; a `$Result` string is not). Also: the fold leaves the entry merge with in-degree 1, which describe->exec would then silently delete, so splice it out in the transform — otherwise Mode 3's output does not describe the graph its own re-execution builds.
